people.name: Tim Bennett
people.bio: Tim Bennett is the Republican nominee and a retired U.S. Army officer who served nearly 30 years and retired in 2018. He was elected in 2025 to the Lewis-Palmer School District 38 Board of Education and lives in Monument.

answers.question: How does your experience make you qualified to represent the people?
answers.answer: My qualifications are centered in a lifetime of service rather than a pursuit of politics. …

answers.question: What are your top policy priorities?
answers.answer: I’m simply committed to improving everyday life for the people of Colorado's CD-7. …

answers.question: What is one issue you think is being overlooked in this race, and how would you address it?
answers.answer: It’s not a single issue that is being looked over. … I simply believe Congress should spend less time representing Washington to Colorado and more time representing Colorado to Washington.

people.name: Brittany Pettersen
people.bio: Brittany Pettersen, a Democrat, is the incumbent U.S. representative for the 7th Congressional District, first elected in 2022, and is seeking a third term. She previously served in the Colorado House of Representatives (2013-2019) and the Colorado Senate (2019-2023). She grew up in and lives in Jefferson County.

answers.question: How does your experience make you qualified to represent the people?
answers.answer: I grew up here in Jefferson County – it's the community that gave me every opportunity to build a better life. As an at-risk youth, I was highly unlikely to graduate high school or college, let alone become a Member of Congress. …

answers.question: What are your top policy priorities?
answers.answer: In Congress, I'm fighting to make sure we have a tax system that works for everyone – not just the ultra-wealthy. At a time when affordability is the top concern I hear from families, we should be investing back in the American people …

people.name: Susan Hall
people.bio: Susan Hall is the Unity Party candidate. She is a teacher who was born and raised in Denver.

people.name: Lawrence Kyle Clark
people.bio: Lawrence Kyle Clark is the American Constitution Party candidate. He is an entrepreneur based in Colorado Springs.

people.name: Dan "Kilo" Sallis
people.bio: Dan "Kilo" Sallis is the Libertarian candidate. He is a small business owner based in Jefferson County.

people.name: Joe Krzeczkowski
people.bio: Joe Krzeczkowski is an unaffiliated candidate and a technology executive who lives in Lakewood. He most recently led a community council in Lakewood and supported the Make Lakewood Livable campaign.

open_questions: FEC: api.open.fec.gov and the fec.gov district search page (/data/candidates/house/?state=CO&district=07...) were blocked (proxy policy / robots), and fec.gov later rate-limited us (HTTP 429). FEC figures above come from individual fec.gov candidate/committee pages. FEC filing status for Susan Hall, Lawrence Kyle Clark and Dan "Kilo" Sallis could NOT be checked; do not state they have no filings until someone checks https://www.fec.gov/data/elections/house/CO/07/2026/ in a browser.

FEC report names: the fetched fec.gov pages showed coverage through 2026-06-30 but not the report name; that coverage end matches the July Quarterly. The October Quarterly (through Sept 30) is due Oct 15 and the Pre-General Oct 22; refresh all FEC figures after those dates.

Questionnaires: CPR News's 2026 CD7 candidate pages are written as CPR summaries of interviews with some short direct quotes, not candidates' written answers, so they are not used as answers. KRDO's profiles (Bennett June 19, Pettersen June 24, 2026) present first-person answers, but the page does not say the candidates submitted them in writing; confirm this if the site needs to. Our fetch tool limits quotes to about 125 characters, so the KRDO answers are trimmed with an ellipsis. An editor could add longer excerpts from the pages.

No 2026 CD7 questionnaire was found from Vote411/LWV, the Colorado Sun, the Denver Post, Colorado Community Media or Colorado Newsline (Colorado Newsline's CD7 guide page https://coloradonewsline.com/voter-guides/contests/2026-general-u-s-house-7th-district/ failed to load). Check again closer to ballot mailing.

Ballotpedia: Joe Krzeczkowski has Candidate Connection answers (key messages on a 'two-tiered justice system', an 'Economy of Abundance' and overturning Citizens United), but the question text did not appear in our fetch, so they are not included. iVoterGuide says Lawrence Kyle Clark completed Ballotpedia's survey, but Ballotpedia blocked our fetches of his page and of Sallis's. Ballotpedia's CD7 race page was a stale pre-primary cache in our fetch.

No endorsements were found for Bennett (his site has no endorsements page), Hall, Clark, Sallis or Krzeczkowski. Krzeczkowski's site shows testimonials from private individuals only. Checks of Republican-aligned groups (NRA-PVF, Club for Growth, U.S. Chamber) did not surface any CD7 2026 endorsement; these groups' lists were not fetched directly.

Susan Hall website: Politics1 lists https://susanhallforcongress.com/, but the site blocked our fetch, and CPR says 'No campaign materials were found at press time.' Politics1 also describes her as a teacher and peace activist who ran in 2012 and 2024. The office she ran for was not verified.

Krzeczkowski: Politics1 lists votejoek.com as his website, while CPR and the campaign use joeforco.com. Politics1 describes Sallis as a 2010 gubernatorial candidate; this was not verified elsewhere, so it is not in the bio. Sallis's site says he has called the district home since 1967.
Lawrence Kyle Clark: no campaign website or questionnaire answers were found. iVoterGuide shows 'Did not answer' on every question.
